name: hugegraph-gremlin-reflected-class
notes: Readiness is polled on the Gremlin endpoint itself, not on /versions or /graphs, for the reason the other two HugeGraph cases record: the engine is a separate process on 8182 that comes up after the REST API answers, so polling 8080's other routes waits for the wrong thing.
This case exists for its control, and the control is the regression for the
defect 3.0.1 fixes. The two halves run the SAME request against the SAME
endpoint and differ only in the method, which is what makes the pair a
class-attribution control rather than two unrelated runs: `eval` reaches
`executed` here honestly -- the endpoint evaluates Groovy without
authentication by design -- and `reflected` must stay `negative`, because
nothing on this endpoint runs a shell.
Until 3.0.1 it did not. One probe shape was a bare `expr a + b` whose
expected value was the sum alone, matched digit-fenced, and Groovy reads
`expr 548286 + 675041` as the command expression `expr(548286 + 675041)`:
it computes the sum, fails to resolve the method, and echoes the result in
its error. So the run printed `executed` under `[reflected/unix/raw]` --
the right tier, filed under a class with no shell in it, which in a client
report is worse than a miss. Measured with every shape mapped before the
fix: 42 probes, `executed=3`, all three that one shape, and 0 of 36 tagged
probes confirming.
`--confirm-depth every` is deliberate and the control is weaker without
it. At the default `first` a carrier stops at its first confirmation, so a
single shape that wrongly confirms can hide behind one that does not run;
mapping every shape is what makes a `negative` here mean every shape was
asked. `--probe-depth full` for the same reason -- `quick` never sent the
defective shape, so a control narrowed to it would have passed throughout.
The vulnerable half duplicates `hugegraph-gremlin-eval`'s invocation on
purpose. A case needs a half that confirms, the runner allows one control
each, and the existing control there is worth keeping: Groovy's own `sleep`
takes milliseconds, so `time` finding no delay is a different boundary.
`share_target` means both cases read one container, so the duplicate half
costs requests rather than a boot.
